title: Video shows 'city-killer' asteroid more powerful than 500 atomic bombs hitting Earth in 2032
text:
An asteroid of ‘city murderer’ now has a 2.3 percent chance of hitting the Earth in about eight years, and a terrifying video has revealed what could happen if it does.
The energy released could be equivalent to eight TNT megatons, capable of devastating an area of ​​the size of Washington, DC.
An explosion of eight megatons would be more than 500 times more powerful than the atomic bomb fallen in Hiroshima, which had a yield of approximately 15 kilotons (0.015 megatons).
The shocking video was created by Álvaro Gracia Montoya, who specializes in 3D animation under the name of Metaballstudios.
It shows a space rock the size of the statue of freedom that burns while falling from heaven and then lands in New York City with amazing force.
The explosive explosion created by the impact quickly wraps and destroys the entire city.
This theoretical asteroid is approximately the same size as asteroid YR4, that astronomers have been closely monitoring since they discovered their slight possibility of directly hitting the earth on December 22, 2032.
When NASA’s telescopes saw for the first time on December 4, 2024, astronomers determined that they had about 1.2 percent of blows on Earth. But now, the chances have almost doubled, according to a recent NASA update.
An asteroid of ‘city murderer’ now has a 2.3 percent chance of hitting the earth in about eight years, and a scary video has revealed what could happen if it does.
The released energy could be equivalent to eight TNT megatons, capable of devastating an area of ​​the size of Washington, DC
This may seem alarming, but the astronomer and professor of planetary sciences at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Richard P Binzel previously told Dailymail.com that small changes like this are nothing to worry about.
‘We can expect the probability numbers to wobble a little. This is how scientific data measurements are developed, “he said.
Other experts have emphasized that an impact probability of 2.3 percent means that there is also a 97.9 percent possibilities that YR4 completely surprise our planet.
When he approaches a nearby approach in 2032, he will reach approximately 66,000 miles of land, which gives him a lot of room for maneuver to pass us.
Even so, this visualization of the damage that YR4 could cause has taken internet by assault.
Online reactions reported by SWNS I have included: “I guarantee that they are already building bunkers underground” and “that will not happen because obviously Bruce Willis and Ben Affleck will go there, will drill a hole on the side and attack it.”
But in the improbable case that the earth hit, its impact might not look like exactly to the horrible scenario that takes place in the animated video of Asteroid Strike. In fact, it cannot even reach the planet’s surface.
Alternatively, it could explode in the air in what is known as an ‘air explosion’, as Tunguska asteroid did in 1908.
Asteroid 2024 years 4 is approximately the same size as the Tunguska asteroid, which caused the greatest impact event in the recorded history when it was shot through the atmosphere of the Earth in 1908
The Tunguska asteroid exploded in the air on Siberia in what is known as an ‘air explosion’, and an explosion equivalent to detonating 50 million tons of TNT that flattened approximately 80 million trees in 830 square miles. Experts say that asteroid 2024 years 4 could cause a similar event

That space rock had approximately the same size as YR4, and caused the most explosive impact on the history registered when it exploded on Siberia.
The force of the explosion was equivalent to detonating 50 million tons of TNT. He flattened approximately 80 million trees in 830 square miles of forest and, according to the reports, killed three people.
Experts say that YR4 can cause a similar event, they need more information about the size, composition and internal structure of the asteroid to understand how its impact can be developed.
As the asteroid approaches, astronomers should be able to make more detailed observations that can help them understand exactly how large is 2024 years 4, what is done and how it meets.
In contrast to the video, it is also unlikely that YR4 touch earth in New York City, or anywhere else in the United States.
According to preliminary data, astronomers have calculated their current ‘risk corridor’, or the geographical area where the asteroid is more likely to arrive.
This area extends from South America through the Atlantic Ocean to sub -Saharan Africa, then through the Arabian and Indian Sea.
Although US cities are excluded from the risk corridor, there are many other densely populated human communities within this area.
The 2024 -year orbit analysis indicates that the asteroid will come to 66,000 miles from the Earth on December 22, 2032. But when the orbital uncertainties are taken into account, it turns out that there is a probability of 1.2 percent that the planet
In addition, experts say that this potential impact zone is subject to changes as astronomers collect new observations and make more precise orbit calculations.
Asteroid 2024 years 4 was first seen by a project funded by NASA called the earthly impact alert system, or Atlas, which uses four terrestrial telescopes to scan the entire sky several times per night looking for mobile objects.
On December 27, 2024, an Atlas telescope located in Río Hurtado, Chile detected the space rock to approximately 27 million miles away.
Shortly after it was discovered, automated asteroid warning systems determined that the object will make an approach close to Earth in approximately eight years.
This space rock has a three rating on Torino’s risk scale, a tool to classify possible Earth’s impact events.
A 2024 year score deserves the attention of astronomers because it is likely to have a close encounter with the Earth and has an impact possibility in more than one percent.
It is a scale from zero to 10, with a greater number that indicates a greater risk of impact.
Most objects close to Earth never reach more than two on the scale.
During the next eight years, astronomers will be closely observing YR4 to monitor the risk that represents our planet. The career to learn everything we can.
